summary: Gambell Airport (GAM) is a vital transportation lifeline for the remote Siberian Yupik village of Gambell on Saint Lawrence Island in the Bering Sea, Alaska. The island sits roughly 200 miles from mainland Alaska and just across the strait from Russia, making the airport one of the only reliable year-round links to the outside world. The facility supports a subsistence-based community and is also a gateway for the island's renowned birdwatching tourism.
faqs:
Q: How do you get to Gambell?
A: You must fly into Gambell Airport, as Saint Lawrence Island has no road or ferry connection to mainland Alaska. Scheduled flights operate from Anchorage, typically with a stop in Nome.

Q: When is the best time to visit Gambell?
A: Summer (June–August) offers the mildest weather and best conditions for the island's famous seabird watching, including puffins, auklets, and murres.

Q: Are there car rentals at the airport?
A: No, there are no rental car agencies at Gambell Airport. The village is compact and most visitors arrange local transportation or ATVs in advance through a host or guide.

Q: What is Gambell known for?
A: The village is known for its Siberian Yupik heritage, subsistence hunting and fishing traditions, and exceptional birdwatching along the island's dramatic sea cliffs.
transport_tips: Flights to Gambell are limited and weather-dependent, so build flexibility into your travel plans and prepare for possible delays. The village has no road network connecting to other communities, so all arrival and departure logistics go through the airport. Pack light and bring essentials, as freight capacity on small aircraft is limited and expensive.
local_tip: Bring binoculars and rain gear even in summer—the seabird colonies on the cliffs near Gambell are world-class, and the weather off the Bering Sea can change in minutes.
